row.basis: spider web woven by evildoers
row.note: The commentary sets firm weaving against the spider's house; Isaiah says wrongdoers weave spider webs, turning the textile image into a judgment on their deeds.

row.basis: web cannot clothe; corrupt works
row.note: The commentary pairs sound fabric with repairing deeds and the frail spider house; Isaiah says their webs cannot serve as clothing because their works are violent, making the failure of the fabric moral as well as material.

row.basis: spider's house as confidence
row.note: The commentary's spider house is a deceptive opposite to firm truth; Job calls the godless person's trust a spider's house, connecting fragile shelter to misplaced confidence.

row.basis: house leaned on but cannot stand
row.note: The commentary contrasts the spider house with a well-founded structure; Job says its owner leans on his house but it will not stand, giving the image its test of load-bearing strength.

row.basis: house building and vain toil
row.note: The commentary sets labor that builds against human loss; the psalm says builders labor in vain unless the Lord builds the house, making a sound structure depend on more than human effort.

row.basis: ع م ل / Hebrew עמל, table sound correspondence
row.note: The source commentary's عمل supplies building labor; Psalm 127 uses Hebrew עמל of builders' futile toil, a pointed cognate comparison because this labor can still be vain.

row.basis: ع م ل / Hebrew עמל, table sound correspondence
row.note: Surah 103 joins human loss to the exception of good work; Ecclesiastes asks what gain a person has from all his עמל under the sun, pressing the same labor-and-gain question without stating that exception.

row.basis: ع م ل / Hebrew עמל, table sound correspondence
row.note: The commentary makes constructive work answer loss; the speaker surveys his works and toil and finds no gain, exposing the opposite outcome for labor considered on its own.

row.basis: ص ل ح / Aramaic צלח, table sound correspondence
row.note: The source labels صالحات as repair against corruption; Ezra reports that the temple rebuilding work advances or prospers in the builders' hands, joining the cognate's different sense to actual constructive work.

row.basis: ص ل ح / Aramaic צלח, table sound correspondence
row.note: The commentary's righteous repair is pictured as building; Ezra says the Jewish elders built and prospered, placing Aramaic צלח inside the completion of a restored house.

row.basis: ص ل ح / Hebrew צלח, table sound correspondence
row.note: The source labels صالحات as deeds that repair; Joshua is told to do the written instruction so his way will prosper, joining action and the Hebrew cognate while retaining its sense of success.

row.basis: ح ق ق / Hebrew חקק, table sound correspondence
row.note: The source's حق includes a door fitting its socket; God says he fixed the sea's prescribed limit and set its bars and doors, using חקק for an imposed boundary rather than ethical truth.

row.basis: ح ق ق / Hebrew חקק, table sound correspondence
row.note: The commentary links truth's firm fit to the broken divine covenant; Leviticus says rejecting God's חקות and judgments breaks that covenant, so the cognate statutes mark exactly what is refused.

row.basis: clasps joining woven curtains into one dwelling
row.note: The commentary's joined pieces and tight fabric make a sound structure; Exodus joins woven curtains with gold clasps so the tabernacle becomes one, a material version of that double image.

row.basis: building or tearing down one's house
row.note: The commentary makes repair and building the opposite of undoing; Proverbs says a wise woman builds her house while a foolish one pulls it down with her own hands.

row.basis: repairer of breach
row.note: The commentary says righteous deeds repair what has been broken; Isaiah calls the obedient community the repairer of a breach and restorer of streets, giving repair a social and built form.

row.basis: two sticks joined into one
row.note: The commentary explains mutual counsel as attaching piece to piece; Ezekiel is commanded to join two named sticks into one in his hand, making reunion visible in an actual joint.

row.basis: threefold cord not quickly broken
row.note: The commentary's thread holds when parts are joined; Ecclesiastes says a threefold cord resists breaking in an argument for companions helping one another.

row.basis: tested cornerstone and secure foundation
row.note: The commentary opposes the firm building to a foundation that collapses; Isaiah lays a tested cornerstone in Zion and says the believer need not panic, joining trust and stability.

row.basis: house built and established by wisdom
row.note: The commentary treats sound truth as a structure assembled through good action; Proverbs says wisdom builds a house and understanding establishes it, giving moral skill a structural result.

row.basis: hearing and doing words builds on rock
row.note: The commentary makes good works and firm truth the basis of a sound house; Jesus likens the person who hears and does his words to a builder founding a house on rock.

row.basis: hearing without doing builds on sand
row.note: The commentary says firm speech requires constructive work; Jesus likens a hearer who does not act to a builder on sand, specifying the defective foundation.

row.basis: great fall of unsound house
row.note: The commentary's ruined foundation ends in loss; Jesus describes the sandy house's fall in the storm as great, giving the construction image its outcome.

row.basis: joints; each part working; body built up
row.note: The commentary joins the bones' meeting place, attached pieces, and useful work; Ephesians says every joint supplies the body as each part works and the body builds itself up.

row.basis: joints and ligaments hold body together
row.note: The source's حق includes the place where bones meet; Colossians says the whole body is supplied and held together by joints and ligaments, making the anatomical join a figure for communal growth.

row.basis: whole building fitted together
row.note: The commentary's door fits its place and each piece is joined; Ephesians says the whole building is joined together and grows into a holy temple.

row.basis: truth spoken because members belong together
row.note: The commentary makes firm truth and attaching parts mutually reinforcing; Ephesians commands truth to one's neighbor on the ground that people are members of one another.

row.basis: speech good for building others up
row.note: The commentary calls firm speech part of communal construction; Ephesians directs speakers to say what is good for building up hearers according to need.

row.basis: house as pillar and support of truth
row.note: The commentary joins a stable house to حق as firm truth; 1 Timothy calls God's household the pillar and support of the truth, making the structural image explicit.

row.basis: one another prompted to good deeds
row.note: The ayah's reciprocal exhortation and good deeds are presented as pieces of one structure; Hebrews asks believers to consider one another so as to stir love and good works.

row.basis: encouraging one another
row.note: The source commentary says recommendation attaches persons like pieces; Hebrews enjoins mutual encouragement in the gathered community, specifying the practice that holds it together.

row.basis: encourage and build one another
row.note: The commentary turns reciprocal counsel into building; the letter commands believers to encourage and build up one another in the same breath.

row.basis: teaching and admonishing one another
row.note: The commentary says tavsiye joins the pieces of a community through sound words; Colossians has the word of Christ dwell in them as they teach and admonish one another.

row.basis: restore a person caught in fault
row.note: The commentary defines صالحات through repair rather than corruption; Galatians directs spiritually minded believers to restore an erring person gently, making repair a communal deed.

row.basis: faith completed by works
row.note: The ayah's believing and doing good are both needed in the commentary's construction; James says Abraham's faith worked with his deeds and was brought to completion by them.

row.basis: living stones built into a spiritual house
row.note: The commentary makes individual deeds into bricks of a common structure; 1 Peter calls believers living stones being built into a spiritual house for worship.

row.basis: firm foundation; inscription; turning from wrong
row.note: The commentary puts firmly set truth beside deeds that repair corruption; this verse joins God's firm foundation and its inscribed seal to a call for everyone naming the Lord to turn from unrighteousness.

row.basis: ص ل ح / Hebrew צלח, table sound correspondence
row.note: The source labels صالحات as constructive deeds; the person delighting in divine instruction is like a planted tree and whatever he does prospers, combining action with the Hebrew cognate's success sense.

row.basis: speak truth to one another; judge truly
row.note: The commentary makes mutual recommendation in حق part of repairing a community; Zechariah commands truth spoken to one another and true judgments in the gates as practices for restored civic life.

row.basis: righteous action and truthful speech
row.note: The commentary places good works beside firm speech; the psalm says the person fit to dwell in God's tent walks blamelessly, does right, and speaks truth from the heart.

row.basis: faithful people speak to one another
row.note: The commentary's reciprocal counsel helps a community avoid loss; Malachi depicts those who fear the Lord speaking with one another while God listens and records their names.

row.basis: joint kept from failing and healed
row.note: The source's حق can name where bones meet while صالح means repair; Hebrews calls for straight paths so a lame limb is not put out of joint but healed, joining both anatomical fit and restoration.

row.basis: no division; members care for each other
row.note: The commentary's joined parts are also people who counsel one another; Paul says bodily members should have no division but equal care for each other.

row.basis: speech in assembly for building up
row.note: The commentary calls firmly formed words part of a common building; Paul requires each contribution to the gathering to be for building up the community.

row.basis: curtains coupled to one another
row.note: The commentary's توصية is a joining of pieces after its woven-cloth image; Exodus prescribes groups of curtains joined to one another, the physical sequence behind a single dwelling.

row.basis: boards coupled below and joined above
row.note: The commentary's fitted door and attached parts build a firm house; Exodus requires the tabernacle's corner boards to be joined at both ends, specifying how the structure holds.

row.basis: wall joined; people had a mind to work
row.note: The commentary compares righteous joint labor to building; Nehemiah describes the wall joined to half its height because the people had a mind to work.

row.basis: truthful speech endures
row.note: The commentary calls محقق speech firm; Proverbs says truthful lips are established forever while a lying tongue lasts only a moment, giving stability an ethical speech test.

row.basis: wise tongue heals
row.note: The commentary links firm speech with repair; Proverbs opposes words that cut like a sword to a wise tongue that heals.

row.basis: righteous house stands when wicked fall
row.note: The commentary's sound structure stands opposite loss; Proverbs says the wicked are overthrown while the house of the righteous stands.

row.basis: righteous person as lasting foundation
row.note: The commentary's foundation comparison distinguishes durable truth from sudden collapse; Proverbs says the wicked vanish in a storm but the righteous are an enduring foundation.

row.basis: justice as line; lies swept from refuge
row.note: The commentary connects a fitted foundation to حق rather than to a merely apparent shelter; Isaiah measures with justice and sweeps away the refuge of lies.

row.basis: false peace and whitewashed wall
row.note: The commentary requires sound speech and sound construction together; Ezekiel condemns those who say peace falsely while coating another's weak wall, a deceptive version of both.

row.basis: whitewashed wall falls in storm
row.note: The source's unstable foundation collapses; Ezekiel announces that the wall covered with whitewash will fall under rain, hail, and wind because its finish did not make it sound.

row.basis: covenant that people broke
row.note: The commentary juxtaposes broken covenant with cut connections; Jeremiah recalls the covenant the people broke despite God's bond with them, naming the breach to be repaired.

row.basis: law written within as renewed covenant
row.note: The commentary's firmly founded word answers covenant rupture; Jeremiah promises God's instruction written on hearts in a renewed covenant, locating durability in the people themselves.

row.basis: ح ق ق / Hebrew חקק, table sound correspondence
row.note: The source calls speech محقق or firmly formed; Isaiah is told to inscribe a warning on a tablet and in a book for lasting witness, showing the cognate's concrete engraving sense.

row.basis: ح ق ق / Hebrew חקק, table sound correspondence
row.note: The source's firm speech is compared with a tightly made object; Job wishes his words engraved in rock forever, using the Hebrew cognate for a physically lasting utterance.

row.basis: ح ق ق / Hebrew חקק, table sound correspondence
row.note: The source's حق makes a door fit its appointed place; Wisdom says God set or prescribed the sea's boundary and marked the earth's foundations, using the Hebrew cognate for fixed order.

row.basis: door turning on hinge
row.note: The commentary singles out the door's foot fitting its socket; Proverbs uses a door turning on its hinge to picture a sluggard stuck in bed, making the same fitted mechanism an image of work withheld.

row.basis: companion lifts one who falls
row.note: The commentary's attached pieces save from loss; Ecclesiastes says one companion can lift the other when he falls, supplying the practical benefit of mutual support.

row.basis: life cut off like woven cloth
row.note: The commentary's sound thread can be undone and lead to loss; Hezekiah portrays his life as a weaver's work cut from the loom, moving the fabric image to mortality.

row.basis: marred vessel remade by potter
row.note: The commentary defines repair as the opposite of spoiling; Jeremiah's potter remakes a spoiled vessel into another, giving an actual artisan's action for that reversal.

row.basis: labor and wages disappearing
row.note: The commentary sets good work against human loss; Haggai says wages go into a bag with holes, making unfruitful labor a tactile image of loss.

row.basis: own houses while God's house lies ruined
row.note: The commentary treats proper building as a moral deed; Haggai says the people's labor yields little because each tends his own house while God's house lies in ruins.

row.basis: bricks made for a common project
row.note: The commentary uses bricks as an image of work that repairs and joins; Babel's people make bricks for a shared tower whose purpose soon proves misguided, so material coordination is not itself righteous.

row.basis: collective building to make a name
row.note: The commentary's tightly joined structure represents truthful, beneficial work; Babel's builders coordinate a city and tower to make a name for themselves, a pointed reversal of the value assigned to cohesion.

row.basis: deeds as roots that keep a tree standing
row.note: Avot interprets the relation of wisdom and deeds through a tree blown by wind: abundant learning with few deeds falls, whereas abundant deeds root it; that sharpens the commentary's claim that firm speech needs constructive action.

row.basis: truth spoken in love grows the body
row.note: The commentary makes حق firm speech within a joined community; Ephesians couples speaking truth in love with growth into Christ, placing truthful words inside the body's construction.

row.basis: foundation and cornerstone
row.note: The source compares sound and collapsing foundations; Ephesians describes the household of God as built on an apostolic and prophetic foundation with Christ as cornerstone.

row.basis: skilled builder and how each builds
row.note: The commentary's builder places bricks as deeds; Paul calls himself a skilled foundation-layer and warns each subsequent builder to consider how he builds on it.

row.basis: each builder's work tested by fire
row.note: The commentary distinguishes structurally sound deeds from apparent construction; Paul says fire will disclose each builder's work, adding a test of workmanship to the building image.

row.basis: community as house if confidence held
row.note: The commentary contrasts a firm house with the spider's fragile refuge; Hebrews calls believers God's house if they hold fast their confidence and hope.

row.basis: exhort one another against hardening
row.note: The commentary's reciprocal counsel holds pieces together against corruption; Hebrews orders daily mutual exhortation lest sin's deceit harden anyone.

row.basis: admonish; help; patience toward all
row.note: The ayah's reciprocal counsel and patience appear together; the letter directs the community to admonish the disorderly, support the weak, and be patient toward all.

row.basis: faith without works is dead
row.note: The commentary places belief beside the labor of doing صالحات; James says faith by itself is dead if it has no works, specifying why a verbal profession does not complete the structure.

row.basis: believers devoted to good works
row.note: The commentary insists belief takes shape in constructive deeds; Titus tells those who have believed God to devote themselves to good works that benefit people.

row.basis: correction can regain a brother
row.note: The commentary treats counsel as joining what is severed; Jesus directs a person to confront a sinning brother privately and says listening gains that brother, a relational repair by speech.

row.basis: seamless tunic woven in one piece
row.note: The commentary's tightly woven cloth serves as a picture of integrity; John's soldiers find Jesus' tunic seamless and woven as one piece, giving a concrete garment whose unity matters in the next action.

row.basis: garment deliberately left untorn
row.note: The commentary quotes the woman who undoes her spun thread; John's soldiers decide against tearing the seamless tunic, preserving a material unity for a different narrative purpose.

row.basis: love binds virtues into completeness
row.note: The commentary says one piece is attached to another to form a firm whole; Colossians calls love the bond of completeness over the listed virtues, translating that join into moral practice.

row.basis: carry one another's burdens
row.note: The commentary makes reciprocal action prevent a part from failing; Galatians tells believers to bear one another's burdens and thereby fulfill Christ's law.

row.basis: wandering person turned back
row.note: The commentary's repair includes restoring a broken connection; James addresses believers who bring back one who has wandered from the truth, joining truth and communal recovery.

row.basis: stones fitted into a tower
row.note: The commentary turns good deeds and attached pieces into a secure building; Hermas sees selected stones fitted into a growing tower, a church image whose individual pieces must be sound.

row.basis: false speech preceding spider webs
row.note: The commentary contrasts sound words with the spider's false shelter; Isaiah first says people trust empty pleas and speak lies, then describes their woven spider webs, linking verbal disorder to the defective fabric.

row.basis: bind truth; write it on the heart
row.note: The commentary joins pieces and makes truth a firm word; Proverbs instructs the hearer to bind loyalty and truth around the neck and write them on the heart, joining attachment and inward durability.

row.basis: faithful person not shaken
row.note: The commentary's firm truth and work should withstand collapse; the psalm concludes that the person meeting its ethical conditions will never be shaken, supplying the stable-dwelling outcome of verse 2.

row.basis: bear with and forgive one another
row.note: The commentary makes repair a reciprocal act that reconnects parts; Colossians orders believers to bear with and forgive one another when a complaint separates them.

row.basis: restoration and mutual encouragement
row.note: The commentary pairs repairing what is spoiled with counsel that joins people; Paul's closing charge asks the community to pursue restoration, encourage one another, agree, and live in peace.

row.basis: perishing hope of the godless
row.note: The commentary's spider house also pictures loss; Job's immediately preceding verse says the godless person's hope perishes, providing the consequence of trusting the frail house in the next verse.

row.basis: scales pressed with no air between
row.note: The commentary's fabric is tightly woven and its pieces fit; the description of Leviathan has protective scales so close that air cannot pass, a concrete compression image with no stated ethical application.

row.basis: scales clinging inseparably
row.note: The commentary says pieces join into a firm whole; Leviathan's scales cling to one another so they cannot be separated, a physical parallel whose role in Job is creaturely strength.

row.basis: life quickly passes with toil and trouble
row.note: Surah 103 names time and human loss while the commentary seeks fruitful work; the psalm compresses human years into toil and trouble before they pass, though it does not develop the construction image.

row.basis: builder suffers loss while escaping
row.note: The commentary's bad foundation carries its builder into loss; Paul says the builder whose work burns suffers loss though the person is saved, a distinct outcome that makes the comparison an uncertain reversal.

row.basis: build yourselves up in faith
row.note: The commentary sees believers' good work as construction; Jude urges the community to build itself up in its holy faith, but supplies no fitted material or foundation in this verse.

row.basis: skin as clothing; bones and sinews knit together
row.note: The commentary combines tightly woven fabric with the place where bones meet; Job addresses God as the one who clothed him with skin and flesh and knit him together with bones and sinews, giving both images one bodily setting.

row.basis: bone joined to its bone
row.note: The source's حق can mean where two bones meet and its counsel joins separated pieces; Ezekiel reports that at the prophetic word the scattered bones came together, bone to its bone, before the bodies lived.

row.basis: dry bones; lost hope; cut off
row.note: The commentary sets joining and repair against loss and severance; the exiles identify themselves as dry bones and say their hope is lost and they are cut off, making the physical reunion of verse 7 answer a declared communal loss.

row.basis: frame intricately woven
row.note: The commentary puts tightly woven fabric beside the meeting of bones; the psalmist describes his bodily frame as intricately woven while hidden in formation, a creation image rather than a moral construction.

row.basis: two workers and reward for toil
row.note: The commentary makes mutual joining and useful work answer loss; Ecclesiastes says two are better than one because their labor has a good reward, grounding the lifting and unbreakable cord described in the following verses.

row.basis: iron sharpens iron; person sharpens person
row.note: The commentary's tavsiye is reciprocal counsel that strengthens a structure; Proverbs describes one person sharpening another as iron sharpens iron, making mutual improvement a material image.

row.basis: foundations destroyed; plight of righteous
row.note: The commentary distinguishes the sound foundation from the one that collapses; the psalm asks what the righteous can do if foundations are destroyed, making structural failure an ethical crisis.

row.basis: raise fallen shelter; repair breaches
row.note: The commentary defines صالح as repairing damage and presents a secure house as its product; God promises to raise David's fallen booth and repair its breaches, making restoration of a ruined dwelling explicit.

row.basis: ع م ل / Hebrew עמל, table sound correspondence
row.note: The commentary asks whether work can answer loss through righteousness; Isaiah's servant comes through the toil of his soul to an outcome that makes many righteous, linking the cognate for painful effort to a fruitful result in this verse's own servant context.

row.basis: ح ق ق / Hebrew חקק, table sound correspondence
row.note: The source sets firm حق beside a covenant that can be broken; Jeremiah says that if God's fixed cosmic statutes depart, Israel will cease as a people, using the cognate for enduring ordinances to secure the restored relationship.

row.basis: hearts encouraged and knit together in love
row.note: The commentary makes reciprocal counsel join parts into one whole; Paul seeks encouraged hearts joined together in love as they reach assured understanding, giving verbal support and cohesion one purpose.

row.basis: deed and truth together
row.note: The commentary joins firm truthful speech to constructive works; the letter urges love in deed and truth rather than words alone, making both elements necessary to a real bond.

row.basis: persist in doing good until harvest
row.note: The ayah joins good deeds with mutual counsel in patience; Galatians tells the community not to tire of doing good because a harvest comes if they do not give up, giving endurance a concrete gain.

row.basis: steadfast labor not in vain
row.note: The commentary opposes durable, beneficial work to loss; Paul calls believers steadfast and abundant in the Lord's work because their labor is not vain, joining firmness, work, and gain.

row.basis: do not tire of doing good
row.note: The commentary makes righteous work something held together by patience; the letter directly tells brothers not to grow weary in doing good, identifying fatigue as a threat to the work.

row.basis: patience in good work
row.note: The surah names good deeds and patient exhortation as the exception to loss; Paul describes those who persist in good work seeking glory and receiving eternal life, linking sustained action to its outcome.

row.basis: body knit in the womb
row.note: The source's woven fabric and joined bones picture sound formation; the psalmist says God knit him in his mother's womb, giving the textile image a personal bodily origin.

row.basis: joined bodies still lacking breath
row.note: The commentary treats joined pieces as part of restoration; Ezekiel sees sinews, flesh, and skin cover the assembled bones, yet says there is no breath in them, qualifying how far physical reconstruction alone goes.

row.basis: work of hands made firm
row.note: The commentary wants labor to yield a durable structure rather than loss under time; the prayer asks God to establish the work of human hands, directly turning transient toil into a request for permanence.

row.basis: unjust house built with unpaid labor
row.note: The source uses a builder's bricklaying for صالح deeds; Jeremiah condemns the man who builds his house unjustly by making a neighbor work without wages, showing that successful construction can embody corruption.

row.basis: stone houses built but not inhabited
row.note: The commentary contrasts sound building with loss; Amos tells oppressors that although they built houses of dressed stone they will not live in them, linking unjust work to forfeited shelter.

row.basis: city built with bloodshed
row.note: The commentary's joined building signifies beneficial action; Habakkuk pronounces woe on the person who builds a town with blood, making the shared construction harmful through its means.

row.basis: peoples labor for fire and nothing
row.note: The commentary sets constructive work against loss; the next verse says peoples toil only for fire and weary themselves for nothing, giving the unjust city's building its fruitless end.

row.basis: Babel builders scattered
row.note: The earlier Babel scene joins people around brickmaking and a tower; God disperses the builders over the earth, completing the counterexample to the commentary's beneficial joining.

row.basis: hands lay foundation and finish house
row.note: The commentary's work places bricks into a sound whole; Zechariah says Zerubbabel's hands laid the temple foundation and will complete it, keeping beginning and completion in the same laboring hands.

row.basis: rebuild ruins and repair devastated cities
row.note: The commentary describes صالح as repair after spoilage; Isaiah says the restored people will rebuild ancient ruins and repair devastated cities, making collective recovery a construction task.

row.basis: enduring righteousness and truthful instruction
row.note: The commentary gives حق the force of something firm and rightly set; the psalm joins God's everlasting righteousness to instruction that is truth, linking durability and moral truth without the fabric metaphor.

row.basis: truthful word and enduring judgments
row.note: The source calls a well-formed utterance firm; the psalm says the sum of God's word is truth and every righteous judgment endures, locating verbal soundness in permanence.

row.basis: word suited to its setting
row.note: The source compares sound speech with a door's foot fitting its socket; Proverbs likens a word spoken at the right time to gold apples in silver settings, giving apt placement an image of material fit.

row.basis: wise rebuke fitted to listening ear
row.note: The commentary's counsel must attach person to person; Proverbs pairs a wise reprover with an ear that listens, comparing the encounter to a gold ornament, so the fit depends on receiving speech.

row.basis: broken staff annulled covenant
row.note: The commentary quotes a divine covenant broken after being bound; Zechariah enacts the opposite direction when the shepherd breaks his staff and thereby annuls his covenant, making the actor and direction of rupture distinct.

row.basis: broken staff annuls brotherhood
row.note: The commentary says cutting what ought to be joined leads to loss; the shepherd breaks a second staff to annul the brotherhood between Judah and Israel, an enacted severance of a social bond.

row.basis: practice greater than exposition
row.note: The commentary insists that firm words become useful through deeds; this teaching says practice is the main thing rather than exposition and cautions against multiplying words, sharpening the distinction between sound speech and empty talk.

row.basis: patience while bearing one another
row.note: The commentary's reciprocal joining must endure strain; Ephesians asks believers to bear with one another in love with humility, gentleness, and patience before urging unity.

row.basis: unity kept in a bond of peace
row.note: The source says recommendation attaches one part to another; Ephesians directs believers to maintain the Spirit's unity in the bond of peace, expressing an ethical joining before its jointed-body image.

row.basis: coworkers and God's building
row.note: The commentary turns individual works into a collective building; Paul calls his fellow ministers God's coworkers and the community God's building, identifying both laborers and structure.

row.basis: foundation that cannot be replaced
row.note: The source compares secure and collapsing foundations; Paul says no one can lay a foundation other than Jesus Christ, specifying why the community's building can be sound.

row.basis: contrasting materials laid on foundation
row.note: The commentary's firm fabric and sound bricks imply that materials matter; Paul lists lasting and combustible materials a builder might place on the foundation, preparing for the fire test in the next verse.

row.basis: endurance after doing God's will
row.note: The ayah names patience alongside good action; Hebrews says believers need endurance so that, having done God's will, they receive the promise, tying perseverance to completed action.

row.basis: do good especially to faith's household
row.note: The commentary treats righteous work as building a community; Galatians urges doing good to everyone, especially the household of faith, identifying the circle in which the work strengthens bonds.

row.basis: stones rejected from the tower
row.note: The commentary's building holds only when its joined pieces are sound; Hermas's tower vision sets rejected stones beside stones incorporated into it, making the fitness of each component morally consequential.

row.basis: small and great bodily members together
row.note: The source compares mutual counsel to parts joined in a body; Clement's discussion of members says the body requires both small and great parts to function together, extending the anatomical image to church order.

row.basis: strong provide for weak
row.note: The commentary's good deeds attach people and repair what is weak; Clement asks strong members to care for weak members and rich ones to supply the poor, giving the jointed body a practical obligation.

row.basis: believers as stones of Father's temple
row.note: The commentary builds a sound structure from its believers' deeds; Ignatius pictures his addressees as stones of the Father's temple raised by the cross, with faith and love involved in their movement.
